q: A ball is projected from level ground with a speed of 15 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. At what time after launch is its velocity perpendicular to the initial velocity? (g = 10 m/s².) (Take sin 37° = cos 53° = 0.6, cos 37° = sin 53° = 0.8.)
s:
Perpendicular means the dot product of v and u is zero.
u = (u cos θ, u sin θ), v = (u cos θ, u sin θ − gt).
u² cos² θ + u² sin² θ − g t u sin θ = 0, so t = {u;g sin θ}.
t = {15;10 × 0.6} = 2.5 s

A ball is projected from level ground with a speed of 55 m/s at 60° above the horizontal. Find its speed when it is 64 m above the ground. (g = 10 m/s².)
Give the answer in m/s, correct to 2 decimal places.
s:
Gravity is the only force, so v² = u² − 2gh whatever the angle.
v² = 55² − 2 × 10 × 64 = 3025 − 1280
v² = 1745
v = 41.77 m/s

q:
A ball is thrown at 5 m/s perpendicular to a smooth incline of angle 37° and later strikes the incline. Find the distance along the incline between the launch point and the point of impact. (g = 10 m/s², sin 37° = cos 53° = 0.6, cos 37° = sin 53° = 0.8.)
(Options are rounded to 2 decimal places.)
s:
Use axes along and perpendicular to the incline. Perpendicular: initial speed 5, acceleration −g cos 37° = −8 m/s².
Time of flight T = {2u;g cos 37°} = 1.25 s.
Along the incline: initial speed 0, acceleration g sin 37° = 6 m/s².
Distance = ½ × 6 × 1.25² = 4.69 m

q:
A 0.1 kg ball is projected at 10 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. Find its kinetic energy at the highest point. (Take sin 37° = cos 53° = 0.6, cos 37° = sin 53° = 0.8.)
Give the answer in J.
s:
At the top the speed is only the horizontal component: v = u cos 37° = 8 m/s.
KE = ½mv²
KE = ½ × 0.1 × 64
KE = 3.2 J

q:
A projectile reaches a maximum height of 20 m and has a horizontal range of 60 m. Find the tangent of its angle of projection.
(Options are rounded to 2 decimal places.)
s:
H = {u² sin² θ;2g} and R = {2u² sin θ cos θ;g}.
Dividing: {H;R} = {tan θ;4}, so tan θ = {4H;R}.
tan θ = {4 × 20;60}
tan θ = 1.33

q:
A ball is projected from level ground with a speed of 50 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. At what time after launch is its velocity perpendicular to the initial velocity? (g = 10 m/s².) (Take sin 37° = cos 53° = 0.6, cos 37° = sin 53° = 0.8.)
Give the answer in s, correct to 2 decimal places.
s:
Perpendicular means the dot product of v and u is zero.
u = (u cos θ, u sin θ), v = (u cos θ, u sin θ − gt).
u² cos² θ + u² sin² θ − g t u sin θ = 0, so t = {u;g sin θ}.
t = {50;10 × 0.6} = 8.33 s

q: A 0.5 kg ball is projected at 20 m/s at 60° above the horizontal. Find its kinetic energy at the highest point.
s:
At the top the speed is only the horizontal component: v = u cos 60° = 10 m/s.
KE = ½mv²
KE = ½ × 0.5 × 100
KE = 25 J

q: A ball is thrown horizontally at 6 m/s from a point on a long smooth incline of angle 37° with the horizontal; it falls on the incline below the point of projection. Find the distance from the launch point to the landing point measured along the incline. (g = 10 m/s², tan 37° = 3/4, tan 53° = 4/3, cos 37° = 0.8, cos 53° = 0.6.)
s:
Take the launch point as origin. The incline is the line y = −x tan 37°.
Ball: x = ut, y = −5t². Landing: 5t² = u t tan 37°, so t = {2u tan 37°;g} = 0.9 s.
Horizontal distance x = 6 × 0.9 = 5.4 m.
Distance along the incline = x ÷ cos 37° = 5.4 ÷ 0.8 = 6.75 m
